rules_text:
Rules summary Game Play Roll die. Collect and place the Beetle matching your die roll into a 4x4 grid. Rolling a 6 allows you to pick any of the 5 available Beetles. 2-Player variant - 5x5 grid. Tools Tools are single use. Magnifying glass - choose any face-up OR face-down Beetle instead of rolling the die. Forceps - Swap 2 beetles tiles in your Jewel Box. Can be used before or after collecting a Beetle. Either - Can be used as either Magnifying Glass or Forceps. Limit to using 1 token per turn. Each unused token at the end of the game is worth 2 points. Scoring Guide Scarabs Score individually. A scarab on the edge adjacent to all different family scores 2 points. A scarab in the middle adjacent to all different family scores 3 points. Weevils Gain points for an unbroken horizontal or vertical line (2 = 3 points, 3 = 6 points, 4 = 10 points). Each weevil can only be counted once. Longhorns If total number of longhorns in your grid is a even number, score 2 for each longhorn. If odd number, score 1 for each longhorn. Ladybugs Score lady bugs which aren't adjacent to another lady bug. 2 = 1 point, 3 = 4 points, 4 = 8 points, 5 = 15 points. Jewels Scores when in non-adjacent pairs, each worth 5 points. More than 2 adjacent to each other - 0 points for all. (Note that in the BGA implementation it seems that all weevils will "try" to be scored: an L-shaped group of 5 weevils will score 9 points (3+2) rather than 10 (4+1).)

I still need to try it in person, so maybe I'll like that better than BGA.

[Rating: 6/10] I love the theme and the artwork, but there is not enough control over my own game to make me want to play this puzzle game again.

[Rating: 6/10] Tile layer where you get a random tile a lot of the time. Just went full circle back to the Carcassonne style of tile placement. The extra bits and bobs you can do definitely add to it, but it just didn't stand out enough as is for me.
